- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward spikes in sentiment; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak if sentiment peaks then declines.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days above 75) and sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overcorrection.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ trend if sentiment is erratic.
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from 1.00 to 0.33), model often lags; adjust forecast to align with 1–2 days of true trend before full reversal.
